Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim

Class QuestNavSimConfig

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim.QuestNavSimConfig
public class QuestNavSimConfig extends Object
Configuration for a SimulatedQuestNav.

The setters are fluent, just as in LimelightSimConfig: 


 var config = new QuestNavSimConfig()
         .withDriftPerMeter(0.005)
         .withRandomizedOrigin(true);

About the error model's default values

They are plausible, not measured. They are chosen so the order of magnitude is reasonable (a well-mounted Quest drifts little) and so the failures show up within a short test. If you have logs from your own headset, tune them; do not treat them as a characterisation of the hardware.

    • withViewfinder

      public QuestNavSimConfig withViewfinder(boolean enabled)
      Switches on the MJPEG viewfinder: a PhotonCameraSim mounted where the headset goes, which renders the field wireframe from its point of view and publishes it over CameraServer.

      It is cosmetic. It does not feed the pose: the Quest localises by visual-inertial odometry, not by seeing AprilTags. It is off by default because it renders with OpenCV on every frame and that costs real CPU.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to switch it on.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withNetworkClient

      public QuestNavSimConfig withNetworkClient(boolean enabled)
      Publishes from a separate NetworkTables instance, connected as a client to the robot's own NT server, instead of writing directly to the global instance.

      Why this option exists

      PoseFrame.dataTimestamp() --- the value you have to feed addVisionMeasurement --- does not come from the protobuf: it comes from the serverTime NetworkTables stamps on each value. And that serverTime is assigned by the server on receipt. When the publisher lives in the same instance as the consumer, ntcore marks the values with the sentinel serverTime = 1, so dataTimestamp() comes out as a constant 1 microsecond and any timestamp-based fusion falls apart.

      With this option on, the simulation reproduces the real topology --- the headset is an NT4 client and the robot is the server --- and the timestamps come out correct, network latency included.

      Why it is off by default

      If the program has no NT4 server listening, the client does not connect and nothing gets published. Publishing with poor timestamps is a degraded failure; not publishing is a total one. In local mode everything else --- pose, tracking, battery, commands --- works the same.

      Switch it on if your robot code fuses on dataTimestamp(), which is the normal case for a pose estimator.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to publish as a network client.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withRandomizedOrigin

      public QuestNavSimConfig withRandomizedOrigin(boolean enabled)
      Starts with the Quest's origin randomly displaced instead of coinciding with the field's.

      It is worth switching on at least once: with the origin at identity, a team that never calls setPose() sees correct field poses by accident, and the bug does not show up until they switch the real headset on.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to randomise it.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.
